1.stem_plain: "He's hardly the person for the job, ___________?" said the manager, shaking his head.

2.stem_plain: During his stay on the farm, all he did was ___________ the farmers plough the field.

3.stem_plain: Catherine's knowledge of computers ___________ so extensive that everybody wants her to be in their project group.

4.stem_plain: The studious boy persevered despite being told that he was making ___________ progress in his work.

5.stem_plain: I am teaching at Everit Enrichment Centre, ___________ is just a stone's throw away from your school.

6.stem_plain: I did not know how long the poor old man ___________ there and decided to offer him a sandwich.

7.stem_plain: "The flight ___________ in half an hour. We had better hurry!" my mother reminded us.

8.stem_plain: The contestant was disqualified for not adhering ___________ the rules and regulations.

9.stem_plain: "Pick what you like. It doesn't have to be something ___________ by us," my parents assured me.

10.stem_plain: ___________ the holiday was a short one, we enjoyed ourselves tremendously.

1.zh: 经理摇头说：“他几乎不是这份工作的合适人选，是吗？”
1.note: hardly 含否定意义，附加问 (Question tag) 用肯定形式 is he。

2.concept: Bare infinitive after all he did was
2.zh: 在农场期间，他所做的就是看农民犁地。
2.note: 固定结构 all he did was + 动词原形 (bare infinitive)。

3.zh: 凯瑟琳的电脑知识非常丰富，大家都想让她加入自己的小组。
3.note: knowledge 不可数，谓语用单数 is。

4.zh: 尽管被告知进步甚微，这个勤奋的男孩仍坚持不懈。
4.note: progress 不可数，用 little；few 修饰可数复数。

5.zh: 我在 Everit 补习中心教书，它离你们学校仅一步之遥。
5.note: 修饰机构名用非限制性定语从句 which。

6.concept: Past perfect continuous — duration before past point
6.zh: 我不知道那位可怜的老人在那里坐了多久，于是决定给他一个三明治。
6.note: 过去某时刻之前持续的动作用过去完成进行时 (Past perfect continuous) had been sitting。

7.zh: “飞机半小时后起飞，我们最好快点！”妈妈提醒道。
7.note: 表时刻表将来用一般现在时 leaves。

8.zh: 该选手因未遵守规章制度而被取消资格。
8.note: 固定搭配 adhere to（遵守）。

9.zh: 父母安慰我说，不必非得选他们挑的东西。
9.note: something 后用过去分词 chosen 表被动修饰。

10.zh: 虽然假期很短，我们仍玩得非常开心。
10.note: 让步从句用 While（虽然）；In spite of 后接名词短语。

11.stem_plain: The pain on my ankle gradually ___________. Soon, I would be able to walk without the aid of a walking stick.

12.stem_plain: After you have a clear idea of the play, we can start thinking about the cast ___________.

13.stem_plain: The young actor ___________ the question by talking about something that was absolutely unrelated.

14.stem_plain: She is always giving orders and expecting others to obey. No one likes her because of her ___________ manner.

15.stem_plain: Tim decided to ___________ and face his fear of water by jumping out of the boat and into the sea.

11.zh: 脚踝的疼痛逐渐消退，我很快就不用拐杖走路了。
11.note: 应选（2）wore off：疼痛减轻。wore on 表拖延；wore out 表耗尽/磨坏；wore away 表磨损。

choices.zh: （时间）消逝，流逝；缓慢过去（动词短语，指时间在不知不觉中一点点过去，通常伴随着让人感到枯燥、漫长或疲惫的语境）
choices.eg: As the boring afternoon lecture wore on, several students found it difficult to stay awake and began to nod off.

choices.zh: （感觉、效果等）逐渐消退，减弱；消失（动词短语，指药物的作用、疼痛感、强烈的情感或某种暂时的状态逐渐减弱直至完全不见）
choices.eg: The local anesthetic administered by the dentist began to wore off about two hours after the tooth extraction procedure.

choices.zh: 磨损，穿坏；使精疲力竭（动词短语，指衣物、鞋子等因长期使用而破损报废，或者因为过度劳累而消耗尽某人的全部体能与精力）
choices.eg: The energetic children completely wore out their parents after a full day of running around the theme park.

choices.zh: 磨损，磨灭；侵蚀，逐渐消失（动词短语，指通过长期的摩擦、风化、水流冲刷等物理作用，使物体的表面或厚度逐渐减少、剥落）
choices.eg: The sharp inscriptions on the ancient stone monument had gradually wore away after centuries of exposure to wind and rain.

12.zh: 清楚剧情后，我们就可以相应地考虑演员阵容。
12.note: 应选（1）accordingly：与计划一致地安排。

choices.zh: 相应地，照着；因此（副词，指根据已经发生、提及或已知的情况、规定、计划，做出与之相匹配、相适应的后续行动或调整）
choices.eg: The flight schedule has been changed due to bad weather, so all passengers must adjust their travel plans accordingly.

choices.zh: 满怀期待地，充满希望地（副词，指因为预料到接下来会有令人兴奋、有趣或重要的事情发生，而表现出极为期待、渴望的神情或举止）
choices.eg: The eager children sat expectantly around the Christmas tree, waiting for their parents to give them permission to open the gifts.

choices.zh: 大概，推测起来；假定（副词，指根据目前已有的常理、迹象或间接证据进行合乎逻辑的推断，认为某事极有可能是真实的，但尚未完全百分之百证实）
choices.eg: The front door is locked and all the lights are switched off, so the neighbors have presumably gone out for dinner.

choices.zh: 同时地，同步地（副词，指两个或两个以上的动作、事件、变化或声音，在同一时间、同一时刻完全并列发生或进行）
choices.eg: The newly upgraded multimedia system allows the teacher's lecture to be broadcast simultaneously to three different seminar rooms.

13.zh: 那位年轻演员谈些毫不相干的事来回避问题。

choices.zh: 提醒，使警觉；向……报警（动词，指将潜在的危险、紧急情况、突发事件或重要警报通知某人，使其提高警惕并做好防范准备）
choices.eg: The smart smoke detector immediately alerted the homeowners to the fire in the kitchen by sending an emergency notification to their phones.

choices.zh: 回避，逃避；躲避（动词，指用机智、狡猾或巧妙的手段去躲过惩罚、法律制裁或责任，或者在谈话中故意绕开不想回答的棘手问题）
choices.eg: The young actor evaded the direct question about his private life by talking about something that was absolutely unrelated to the topic.

choices.zh: 转移，目光移开；避免，防止（动词，指为了不看某物而转开目光或视线，或者采取果断行动去阻止、防范某种灾难或糟糕局面的发生）
choices.eg: The quick wit and swift action of the alert school bus driver managed to avert what could have been a catastrophic multi-vehicle highway accident.

choices.zh: 逃脱，逃跑；逃避（现实）（动词，指成功从被囚禁、被限制、危险或不快乐的状态中挣脱出来，重新获得自由，或者指物品或名字被遗忘）
choices.eg: The laboratory workers were thoroughly relieved to find that none of the venomous snakes had escaped from their securely locked glass enclosures.

14.zh: 她总是发号施令，要别人服从，没人喜欢她专横的态度。

choices.zh: 仓促的，草率的；匆忙的（形容词，指行动、决定或判断在时间极其紧迫、未经深思熟虑或缺乏足够准备的情况下做出，因而极易出错）
choices.eg: A hasty decision to sign the business contract without reading the fine print led to severe financial mistakes on the final order form.

choices.zh: 鲁莽的，不顾后果的（形容词，指人的行为或做事方式极其大意、危险，完全不在乎可能对自己或他人生命财产造成的严重伤害或后果）
choices.eg: The reckless driver was severely punished by the traffic police for speeding through a crowded school zone during the busy morning rush hour.

choices.zh: 冲动的，凭一时冲动的（形容词，指人受到瞬间的情绪、欲望或突然的念头驱使而做出的举动，完全没有事先计划或考虑长远的影响）
choices.eg: Buying that highly expensive luxury watch on a whim was an impulsive decision that the young executive later regretted deeply when his bills arrived.

choices.zh: 专横的，傲慢的；颐指气使的（形容词，指一个人的态度或做事方式非常傲慢、强硬，习惯于高高在上地向他人发号施令并强迫别人服从）
choices.eg: She is always giving orders to her colleagues and expecting everyone to obey her without question; no one likes working with her because of her imperious manner.

15.zh: 蒂姆决定硬着头皮，跳下船入海，直面对水的恐惧。
15.note: 应选（1）bite the bullet：勇敢面对不愿做的事。

choices.zh: 咬紧牙关，硬着头皮去执行；勇敢面对（动词短语，指在面对无法逃避的痛苦、艰难、不情愿或长期恐惧的局面时，下定决心、鼓起勇气去面对和解决）
choices.eg: Tim decided to bite the bullet and face his lifelong fear of water by jumping straight out of the boat and into the deep sea.

choices.zh: 复出，东山再起；重振旗鼓（动词短语，指在经历失败、重伤、隐退或长期低迷之后，重新获得成功、恢复往日的名望、地位或流行度）
choices.eg: After undergoing a major knee surgery and months of intense physical therapy, the veteran tennis star managed to make a brilliant comeback by winning the tournament.

choices.zh: 经得起时间的考验，历久弥新（动词短语，指某种思想、艺术作品、文学名著或人际关系质量极高，在经历长久的时间流逝或时代变迁后依然具有价值、广受欢迎）
choices.eg: The teacher explained that classical literature pieces survive the test of time because their core themes about human nature remain deeply relevant to readers today.

choices.zh: 启动某事，开动机器；让计划开始运转（动词短语，指采取了第一个关键性的实际行动，从而触发一系列连锁反应，使某个大型计划、活动或法律程序正式开始运作）
choices.eg: The project coordinator submitted the official budget proposal to the board of directors, which finally set the wheels in motion for the construction of the new school wing.

16.note: 形容词 placid 意为平静的、安详的。在描写患者情绪稳定、毫无波动的医学考查语境中，它直接对应高频形容词 calm（平静的，冷静的，镇定的）。

choices.zh: 平静的，冷静的，镇定的
choices.eg: The consulting doctor noticed that the patient stayed exceptionally calm throughout the clinical evaluation.

choices.zh: 茫然的，神志恍惚的
choices.eg: Following the sudden traffic accident near the school gate, the driver looked completely dazed.

choices.zh: 疲惫的，疲劳的
choices.eg: The exhausted marathon runner felt heavily fatigued after ascending the steep mountain trail.

choices.zh: 紧张的，焦虑的
choices.eg: It is perfectly normal for primary school pupils to feel slightly nervous before their formal examinations.

17.note: 名词 evaluation 在医学或精神科语境中指对病情的全面评估与分析。及物名词 diagnosis 意为诊断，在指代判定某种特定病症的核心学术考点中最为对标。
17.zh: 医生心想这男孩可能需要精神科诊断。

choices.zh: 发现，发掘
choices.eg: The prominent research group made a brilliant scientific discovery that could revolutionize clinical medicine.

choices.zh: 诊断，诊断书
choices.eg: The experienced psychiatrist provided a clear diagnosis regarding the child's sudden cognitive condition.

choices.zh: 判断，判断力，判决
choices.eg: When navigating a volatile layout emergency, you must rely heavily on your professional judgement.

choices.zh: 调查（指对案件、事故的深入探查）
choices.eg: The local authorities launched a thorough investigation to ascertain the exact cause of the laboratory explosion.

18.concept: 近义词 — Without further delay（立刻）
18.note: 短语 Without further delay 意为毫不耽搁、立刻做某事。副词 Instantaneously 意为瞬间地、即刻地，两者在修饰动作发出极快的迅速程度上属于直接近义代换。
18.zh: 陈医生立刻走过去自我介绍。

choices.zh: 不耐烦地，焦躁地
choices.eg: The supervisor tapped his fingers impatiently while waiting for the assistant to compile the missing files.

choices.zh: 本能地，凭直觉地
choices.eg: The mother reacted instinctively and pulled her little brother away from the hot kitchen counter.

choices.zh: 同时地，并行地（指两个或多个事件同步进行）
choices.eg: The university scheduled the two workshop events concurrently, making it hard for students to attend both.

choices.zh: 立刻，瞬间，即刻
choices.eg: As soon as the technician entered the command, the entire system layout updated itself instantaneously.

19.concept: 近义词 — dramatic outburst（剧烈发作）
19.note: 短语 dramatic outburst 意为情绪或病症的剧烈、夸张的发作。在医学和心理学描述病情突发加重的上下文逻辑中，短语 an exaggerated flare-up 意为（疾病/痛苦的）夸张暴发、剧烈发作，与其最接近。
19.zh: 他从未见过如此剧烈的歇斯底里失明发作。

choices.zh: 不寻常的暴发（多指传染病或战争等大范围出现）
choices.eg: The world environmental health organization monitored an unusual outbreak of a rare flu virus across the region.

choices.zh: 意外激增，突发高涨
choices.eg: The online grocery platform recorded an unexpected surge in demand for organic products during the lockdown.

choices.zh: （病情/愤怒等的）夸张爆发，剧烈发作
choices.eg: The specialist had never witnessed such an exaggerated flare-up of hysterical blindness in his career.

choices.zh: 失控的喷发（多用于火山等物理破坏性喷涌）
choices.eg: The volcano showed signs of an uncontrollable eruption, forcing local residents to leave their homes.

20.note: 副词 nonchalantly 意为若无其事地、漫不经心地。副词 casually 意为随意地、淡然地，在描写人物回应他人时展现出的不在乎、无所谓的态度时，完全同义。
20.zh: “哦，”她漫不经心地说，“从你挡住电视起就这样了。”

choices.zh: 乐意地，欣然地，轻易地
choices.eg: She was exceptionally kind and readily agreed to help her teammate format the database payload.

choices.zh: 漫不经心地，随意地，淡然地
choices.eg: “Oh,” she stated casually, “he has been acting strange ever since you blocked his view of the television.”

choices.zh: 随意地，随机地，任意地
choices.eg: The computer system was programmed to select three candidate names randomly from the extensive database.

choices.zh: 自信地，胸有成竹地
choices.eg: She walked onto the grand stage and spoke confidently about her breakthrough in green technologies.

cloze: Dr Tan strolled into the hospital ward. As he approached the boy who was sitting on his bed, the doctor noticed that the patient seemed to show an unusually [Q16 (placid)] temperament. "Looks like this young man can do with a psychiatric [Q17 (evaluation)]," he mused. A middle-aged lady was seated next to the bed, but she was totally engrossed in her knitting. [Q18 (Without further delay)], Dr Tan walked over and introduced himself. The boy, however, looked right through the doctor and all of a sudden, broke into a piercing scream. "I can't see! I can't see!" Never in his life had he ever witnessed such a [Q19 (dramatic outburst)] of hysterical blindness. "How long has this been going on?" he asked the lady, unable to comprehend the boy's peculiar behaviour.
"Oh," she said [Q20 (nonchalantly)]. "Ever since you stepped in front of the television."
zh: 陈医生走进病房。走近床上的男孩时，他注意到病人显得异常平静。医生心想这男孩或许需要精神科评估。床边坐着一位中年女士，却全神贯注地织毛衣。陈医生立刻上前自我介绍。男孩却像没看见医生，突然尖叫：“我看不见了！我看不见了！”医生从未见过如此剧烈的歇斯底里失明发作，便问女士这种情况持续多久，无法理解男孩的古怪行为。
“哦，”她漫不经心地说，“从你挡住电视起就这样了。”

21.stem_plain: What is the **main** purpose of the flyer on page 6?

options.1: To raise funds for underprivileged children
options.2: To look for students who can take care of animals
options.3: To encourage people to volunteer or make donations
options.4: To heighten the awareness of the needs of the elderly

22.stem_plain: How is Twilight Dreams Home similar to Hercules Physiotherapy Centre?

options.1: They take care of the elderly.
options.2: They look for helpers who can dance.
options.3: They receive donations from the public.
options.4: They recruit volunteers for Sunday programmes.

23.stem_plain: Mindy is eleven years old. She wants to volunteer on a Saturday for two hours with her mother. They can volunteer at ___________.

24.stem_plain: Fourteen-year-old Raja can volunteer up to three hours on a single Sunday on his own. He can ___________.

options.1: read to children in the hospital
options.2: clean cages at the animal shelter
options.3: collect donations for the physiotherapy centre
options.4: play chess with the elderly at the senior home

25.stem_plain: The brackets used on page 6 serve to ___________.

options.2: add more details to the information
options.4: allow readers to retrieve important information

26.stem_plain: Which of the following is what Aunty Marie likes most when young volunteers visit her?

options.4: being taught to use the mobile phone

27.stem_plain: The three testimonials provided by Aunty Marie, Miss Cecil Lee and Miss Dawn Chua tell us ___________.

options.1: the types of activities they enjoy doing
options.2: why people sign up to help the elderly
options.3: who they like to spend their weekends with
options.4: how volunteers or donations have helped them

28.stem_plain: According to Miss Cecil Lee, some of the animals that are taken to the animal shelter ___________.

options.3: need the staff at the shelter to train them
options.4: are given therapy sessions by volunteers

21.note: The Gifts SG flyer invites people to volunteer or donate to partner organisations — option (3).

22.note: Both Twilight Dreams Home and Hercules Physiotherapy Centre receive donations from the public — (3).

23.note: Mindy is 11; Saturday two hours with mother → Precious Paws Animal Shelter fits age/day rules — (3).

24.note: Raja, 14, up to three hours Sunday alone → play chess with the elderly at the senior home — (4).

25.note: Brackets on the flyer add more details to the main points — (2).

27.note: They show how volunteers or donations have helped beneficiaries — (4).

28.note: Miss Cecil Lee: some animals arrive unwell and need therapy — (2).

cloze: Imagine this — you are sinking your teeth into a delectable cheeseburger, complete with buttery buns, tangy pickles and a succulent beef patty. As you let the textures and flavours dance [Q29] on your taste buds, the chef comes up to [Q30] and introduces the burger: it is the restaurant's first ever meat-free, laboratory-grown burger.
You cannot believe your ears. How [Q31] burgers be grown in a laboratory?

In 2013, scientists extracted cells [Q32] a cow and artificially developed muscle tissue. [Q33], they made the rest of the burger with other preservatives. [Q34] cultivating billions of cells, the first laboratory-grown burger was created. Despite [Q35] less-than-stellar taste reviews, the creation was certainly a huge step forward in the efforts of food production. Why would anyone go to such lengths to produce food? One [Q36] wonder. The reason is that our current system of food production is simply not sustainable.

With the global population expected to grow [Q37] between two and nine billion by 2050, our existing arrangement will not suffice. Massive acres of land are needed to grow crops and farm animals. Reducing the world's cattle herds [Q38] significantly reduce carbon emission of methane, a greenhouse gas, that contributes to global warming. These concerns are pressing enough to demand an alternative solution to food production.
zh: 想象一下——你正咬一口美味芝士汉堡：黄油面包、酸黄瓜、多汁牛肉饼。当口感与味道在舌尖萦绕时，厨师走过来介绍：这是餐厅首份实验室培育的“无肉”汉堡。
你简直不敢相信：汉堡怎么能在实验室里种出来？
2013 年，科学家从牛身上提取细胞并人工培育肌肉组织，随后又用其他添加物完成汉堡其余部分。在培育数十亿个细胞之后，首个实验室汉堡诞生了。尽管评价平平，这无疑是食品生产的一大进步。为何有人不惜代价？人们或许会问——因为现行食品生产体系不可持续。
全球人口预计到 2050 年将增至二十亿至九十亿，现有模式难以为继。大量土地用于种植作物与饲养牲畜；减少牛群数量可显著降低甲烷排放，从而缓解全球变暖。这些紧迫问题促使人们寻找替代方案。

29.note: flavours dance around on your taste buds 表在味蕾上萦绕。故填'C — around'。

30.note: the chef comes up to you 第二人称。故填'Q — you'。

31.note: How could burgers be grown in a laboratory? 表可能性。故填'D — could'。

32.note: extracted cells from a cow 表来源。故填'F — from'。

33.note: Subsequently, they made the rest of the burger 表随后。故填'M — subsequently'。

34.note: After cultivating billions of cells 表在……之后。故填'A — after'。

35.note: Despite its less-than-stellar taste reviews 指实验室汉堡。故填'H — its'。

36.note: One might wonder 表'人们或许会想'。故填'K — might'。

37.note: grow anywhere between two and nine billion 表在……之间任何幅度。故填'B — anywhere'。

38.note: Reducing herds will significantly reduce carbon emission 表将来结果。故填'P — will'。

cloze: Welcome to secondary school life! I know it is quite [Q39(unnerveing)] the first time you step into school as the [Q40(envirroment)] here is very different from the previous one you have experienced.

You must be [Q41(overwhelm)] by the number of subjects you need to take. But I am sure that you will learn to adapt and [Q42(asimillate)] into our school culture in no time. [Q43(Despite)] the school hours are longer, we still have to make time for [Q44(excercize)] and play. School life is more than just about homework and exams, isn't it?

As [Q45(adoulescents)] , we may get bored more [Q46(easy)] than adults do. Hence, activities like sports, games and the arts help to build character. While [Q47(participate)] in sports tone our muscles, they also teach us [Q48(resillance)] . This is how we develop into better people and become an inspiration [Q49(towards)] others.
At the same time, we also get to make new friends! [Q50(Believing)] me, life in secondary school is more bearable when you have friends to appreciate and support you.
I wish you all the best in your secondary school life!
zh: 欢迎来到中学生活！我知道第一次踏进校门会令人紧张，因为这里的环境与你以往经历的截然不同。你可能被众多科目压得喘不过气，但我相信你会很快适应并融入我们的校园文化。尽管在校时间更长，我们仍要抽时间锻炼与玩耍。学校生活不只是作业和考试，不是吗？作为青少年，我们可能比成年人更容易感到无聊，因此体育、游戏与艺术有助于塑造品格。参与运动既能强健肌肉，也教会我们韧性，从而成为更好的人并激励他人。同时我们还会结交新朋友！请相信我，有朋友欣赏与支持，中学生活会好受得多。祝你们中学一切顺利！
你也许会被必须修读的众多科目压得喘不过气。但我相信你会很快学会适应，并融入我们的校园文化。尽管在校时间更长，我们仍要抽时间锻炼和玩耍。学校生活不只是功课和考试，不是吗？
作为青少年，我们可能比成年人更容易感到无聊。因此，体育、游戏和艺术等活动有助于塑造品格。参与运动既能锻炼肌肉，也教会我们韧性；我们借此成长为更好的人，并成为他人的榜样。
同时，我们还能结交新朋友！请相信我，有朋友欣赏与支持，中学生活会好受得多。
祝你们中学生活一切顺利！

cloze: Arch back and stand tall. Blend in with the surroundings. Run. [Q51] are just some of the ways that animals protect [Q52] in the wild. Some of these means of protection are well known. [Q53] are more subtle or downright bizarre. For example, some species of ants will self-explode to protect their [Q54]. This protective action kills the ants but it can [Q55] the colony from danger. The Texas horned lizard will squirt blood from its eyes at a predator to keep [Q56] safe. A sea cucumber expels its protective organs from its anus to protect itself and in some cases, the sea cucumber's intestines can be [Q57] to predators, thus effectively killing them. These defence mechanisms may seem wild but they are crucial in [Q58] the survival of animals and their own kind. For animals to live [Q59] enough to reproduce and continue their species, they often need ingenious strategies.

There are many different [Q60] in which animals protect themselves from predators. However, no one defence mechanism is always effective as predators occasionally find new ways to defeat it. Hence, many animals use [Q61] than one defence mechanism at a [Q62]. For example, the hognose snake has camouflaged colours that help it [Q63] detection by predators but if an owl or some other predator finds it, the hognose snake will inflate its neck to trick the predator so as to appear [Q64] than it is. If this does not work, the hognose snake will [Q65] dead. Every species has its own bag of survival tricks.
zh: 弓背站立、融入环境、奔跑——这些都是动物在野外保护自己的方式。有些手段众所周知，有些则更隐蔽甚至古怪。例如某些蚂蚁会自爆以保护蚁群：此举虽杀死蚂蚁，却能保护群体免遭危险。德州角蜥会从眼中喷血吓退捕食者；海参从肛门排出器官自卫，有时肠道对捕食者有毒。这些防御机制看似疯狂，却对动物及其同类的生存至关重要。动物要活得足够长久才能繁殖延续，往往需要巧妙策略。
动物防捕食的方式多种多样，但没有一种机制永远有效，捕食者偶尔会找到新办法破解。因此许多动物会同时使用不止一种防御。例如猪鼻蛇的体色有助于躲避天敌，若仍被发现，它会胀颈让自己显得更大；若仍无效，便会装死。每个物种都有自己的生存绝招。

51.note: 句首用以总括并承接前文三个短促的动作指令（弓背、站直、隐蔽、奔跑）。指代“这些（These）”就是野生动物自我保护的诸多手段，位于句首需大写。

52.concept: 反身代词与主语人称一致
52.note: 主语为复数名词 animals（动物）。根据主语与宾语为同一主体的语法规则，作动词 protect 的宾语必须填入复数反身代词 themselves，意为保护“它们自身”。

53.note: 修饰复数谓语动词 are。前文提到了一些手段广为人知（Some... are well known），此处与之形成平行的对比与代指，指出“另一些（others / some）”则更为隐蔽或怪异。位于句首需大写。

54.concept: 名词语意与后文复现呼应
54.note: 由形容词性物主代词 their 修饰。后文句子紧接着提到了 from danger 的承受主体是 the colony（蚁群），属于典型的“后文专属名词复现”线索提示，故此处必然对应填入名词 colony / nest / home / community。

55.note: 前面有情态动词 can，后接动词原形。指工蚁自爆虽然导致自身死亡，却能“拯救（save）”、“保护（protect）”或“免除（keep/shield）”整个蚁群脱离危险，故填入动词原形。

56.note: 主语为单数第三人称特指动物 The Texas horned lizard（得州角蜥）。作形容词补足结构 keep... safe 的宾语，根据前后视角一致原则，必须填入单数代词 itself 来代指保护“它自己”。

57.concept: 形容词与介词特定搭配
57.note: 作为系动词 can be 之后的表语，后接介词短语 to predators。在探讨海参喷出内脏御敌的生物学场景下，指其肠道和内脏对捕食者而言是“有毒的（poisonous/toxic）”或“致命的（fatal/lethal）”，从而能有效毒杀天敌。

58.concept: 介词后的动名词与功能搭配
58.note: 介词 in 后面需要接动名词（V-ing）形式。指这些离奇的防御机制在“确保（ensuring/securing）”、“保护（protecting）”或“协助（helping/aiding）”动物种群延续中起着至关重要的作用。

59.concept: 时间修饰副词与固定句型
59.note: 后接修饰限定词 enough to reproduce。完美契合形容生命跨度与繁衍前提的经典习惯表达 live long enough，表示动物们必须活得“足够久”才能繁育后代。

60.concept: 名词语意修饰与前文复现
60.note: 前面有形容词 different 修饰。呼应全篇开篇第一句出现的 ways 概念，指动物们保护自己免受捕食者侵害有许多种不同的“方式”、“手段”或“途径”，故填复数名词 ways / means / methods / strategies。

61.note: 后接比较连词 than one defence mechanism。完美契合数量多重组合的极高频固定结构 more than one（不止一种/多于一种），指许多动物会同时动用多重防御机制。

62.concept: 时间名词习语固定搭配
62.note: 与前置的介词短语 at a 完美组合。构成在各类科学行为和描述中极其核心和高频的专属频率习语 at a time，意为在同一时间/“一次”动用不止一种防御机制。

63.concept: 助动词后的动词原形与专属搭配
63.note: 使役动词结构 help it... 后面接动词原形。与后面的名词宾语 detection（侦测/发现）完美组合，指猪鼻蛇的保护色能够帮助它“躲避（avoid/escape/evade/elude）”捕食者的双眼。

64.concept: 形容词比较级句型形式
64.note: 后接比较连词 than it is。指猪鼻蛇会通过给颈部充气来威吓天敌，从而让自己看起来比实际体型“更大”或“更吓人”，故填形容词比较级 bigger / larger / scarier / fiercer。

65.concept: 短语动词经典习语搭配
65.note: 前面有情态动词 will，后接动词原形。与后面的形容词 dead 完美组合，构成在各类动物科普、大自然纪录片里极其核心和高频的专属拟态伪装习语 play dead，意为“装死/诈死”。

paragraphs.1: 某个周六早上七点前，体育场外已聚满人群。大卫坐在起跑线上，戴着手套紧握轮椅。他心跳加速，担心自己能否跑完全程。同学们都来支持他；远处可见他们举着横幅高喊：“大卫，我们与你同在！一路为你加油！”他备受鼓舞，微笑着挥手回应，决心不辜负大家。
paragraphs.7: 大卫生来患有严重疾病，腰部以下瘫痪，许多医生认为他活不过几天。然而他战胜一切，在孤儿院度过生命最初六年，没有轮椅也没有医疗照顾。他回忆道：“若想像其他孩子一样，就得靠自己。”六岁时被收养，此后发生许多事：养父母安排多次手术改善状况，他得以上学并参加运动强健筋骨，继而爱上轮椅竞速。可惜他协调与力量不足，但仍坚持前行；有一次病情毫无预警地恶化，几乎毁掉他对这项热爱的追求。
paragraphs.18: 一天，老师鼓励他与非轮椅同学一起比赛。他既忐忑又感激，决定试一试。开赛时太阳已升起，他庆幸自己准备充分：调整头上的帽子和手套，做好防晒并减轻划轮椅对手部的冲击；部分手指贴着胶布，保护训练磨出的水泡。他注视着挥红旗的发令员；枪响后大卫冲出，全场爆发出雷鸣般的欢呼。
paragraphs.27: 大卫全力向前，双手全程紧握轮子进行长跑。轮椅平稳驶出体育场，经过店屋。尽管竭尽全力，他仍落在其他选手后面。时间一小时一小时过去，他呼吸越来越急促，每一次划动都让手臂和肩膀剧痛，但他仍专注地坚持。
paragraphs.33: 头顶烈日当空，大卫精疲力竭、口干舌燥，头仿佛着火，阳光透过帽子灼烧着他，那正在消耗他的体力，他开始虚弱疲惫。继续推进时，滚烫的金属轮缘灼痛双手，但他从未想过停下，只依靠自己能掌控的东西——态度。火球是他的敌人，如同挡在路上的种种障碍——疼痛、残疾与对失败的恐惧，但他决心一一克服。
paragraphs.41: “加油，大卫！”人群再次呐喊。大卫向前猛冲，仿佛以不可阻挡的速度飞翔。明黄色的终点带越来越近，他冲过彩带，全场响起胜利的欢呼。
